messages:
lucas: paging oncall — alert: streaming tail p99 spike on prod, started ~09:12 UTC. Ops bot fired: SLO p99 breach (streaming). seeing user-facing stalls and a few 504s.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: stream-service.p95=1.2s (baseline 110ms), p99=3.4s, errors=2.3% over 5m. Paging: @sre_rotation, @maria

sre_rotation: I'm on it. quick check — which stacks? ingest->preproc->tokenizer->serve?

lucas: exactly. initial graphs point to preproc/tokenizer queueing; traces show long `prompt_hydration` spans when requests use JSON-mode and tool-schema rendering.

ada: adding logs from the affected host: ```
2026-03-15T09:11:45Z INFO request_id=abc123 prompt_mode=JSON render_time_ms=870 template_expansions=12 tokenizer_enqueue_ms=450
2026-03-15T09:11:46Z WARN request_id=def456 streaming_stall_ms=1200 kv_cache_hit=false
```

jonathan: re: template_expansions=12 — did we just ship the new dynamic tool-schema expansion in templates? I think that increases tokenization work for some routes.

maria: yeah we rolled `tool-schema-injector` at 08:40 UTC behind flag. traffic to enterprise-route A is hitting it.

lucas: customer impact: a handful of large customers (ent-A, ent-B) reported slow responses and a couple timed out. Support tickets open. severity S3 (customer-impacting for multiple users).

ada: metrics: chunking/ops per request up ~3.5x for JSON-mode requests, tokenizer CPU for preproc pods at 82% with long GC pauses. p95 latency for prompt-constructor jumped from 120ms -> 1.05s.

sre_rotation: immediate mitigation plan: 1) roll back `tool-schema-injector` flag for the enterprise routes, 2) enable prompt_template_cache, 3) scale preproc pod HPA + add instance hot spares, 4) fallback route to older prompt renderer for streaming when KV-cache misses > 50%.

maria: I'll take rollout rollback and coordinate with deploys. calling the deploy bot now.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: start rollback job (#4567) for `tool-schema-injector` -> canary -> all. ETA ~4m.

lucas: while rollback is in progress, enable `prompt_template_cache` via runtime flag on preproc cluster. This should cut repeated template rendering. ada — can you flip?

ada: flipping `prompt_template_cache=true` on preproc pool now. ```sh
kubectl patch cm preproc-config -p '{"data":{"prompt_template_cache":"true"}}'
```

ada: flipped. cache warmup will take a couple minutes.

jonathan: also reducing `max_template_expansions` to 8 as a safety cap. pushed config change.

maria: rollback completed on enterprise-route canary -> monitoring for drop in p99. opsbot shows canary success.

ops-bot: ROLLBACK: `tool-schema-injector` rollback completed for canary (ok). Promoting rollback to 100% in 2m.

lucas: metrics update 09:22 UTC: p95 down from 1.2s -> 400ms, p99 down from 3.4s -> 1.1s. errors trending down. streaming stalls still ~3% on tail.

sre_rotation: good progress. next: dig traces for remaining tail requests. are stalls correlated with KV-cache misses?

ada: yes — samples show streaming stalls correlate strongly with `kv_cache_hit=false` and large `template_expansions`. enabling cache reduced duplicate work.

maria: handoff: I need to step into customer calls in 20m. lucas, you continue triage + RCA and coordinate with support for impacted customers. I'll be primary incident liaison until I'm back.

lucas: taking over. tagging follow-ups: - deep root cause: template + tool-schema expansion increased tokens and heavy prompt-constructor CPU. - immediate rollback + cache reduced surface impact. - next steps: add guardrails, improve feature-flag rollout docs, add unit test for expansion explosion, and provide customer postmortem.

ada: action items assigned in incident board: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4509876543 — I'll attach traces and flamegraphs.

jonathan: long-term: consider precomputing tool-schema expansions (offline) and storing canonical compact form in KV store to avoid per-request expansion. also, better quotas on template complexity.

ops-bot: NOTE: Maintaining elevated logging for preproc for next 2 hours. Disk and CPU autoscale monitored.

lucas: final update 09:46 UTC: p95 ~160ms, p99 ~210ms, errors <0.2%, streaming stalls under threshold. lowering page severity. I'll keep monitoring for 2h.

maria: thanks team. I'll compile customer impact notes and join post-incident review tomorrow. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: incident reassigned to lucas for monitoring; oncall cleared to standby.

lucas: putting a short postmortem draft in docs and will link once ready.

ada: adding sample flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/flame/4509876543
